correctness.rationale: Detailed balance holds pairwise and the zero-sum slow/fast modes decay with rates a and ar+c(1-r), with orthogonality in the stationary-weighted norm. Initially the squared weighted norm plus one is Z(beta_b)Z(2beta-beta_b)/Z(beta)^2, strictly decreasing toward the bath by strict monotonicity of the Gibbs mean energy. TV initially is the maximum of the falling ground-state deficit and falling upper-state surplus. The fast amplitude n has strictly decreasing temperature-parameter dependence in beta because q2 decreases and q0 increases. Thus the weighted squared-distance difference after removing its common exponential is strictly increasing in z^2. The rescaled TV difference is constant before either hinge, possibly decreasing if warm activates alone, then strictly increasing from the hot activation onward (or increasing through both segments if hot activates first). With the strict slow-amplitude inequality and the initial ordering there is one genuine root for each metric. The middle Gibbs mass derivative changes sign at most once, and a strictly ascending part with q1 above the bath value is available exactly when E>2 Delta and beta_b>beta_*, giving the supporting boundary on the stated nonnegative domain. An independent rational computation projected the forward generator onto its modes and solved the unsquared absolute-value difference between coordinate breakpoints. The computed pairs (z2^2,zTV) were (8180/3657833,4259/126087) and (228877/138852250,2816/24875), with opposite nonzero signs of z2^2-zTV^2, giving the claimed time orders since z decreases with time.
residual_risks: Within each witness the two preparations use the same generator. Across witnesses the generators differ with the bath; the energy levels and prefactors, not all transition rates, are held fixed.

value.rationale: Opposite exact root orders, with a unique true crossing of both metrics in each witness, rule out a universal schedule ordering between two standard norms even within a single three-level rate form and canonical temperatures. The result distinguishes occurrence of a Mpemba effect from what time either diagnostic reports, with strict margins certified independent of numerical precision.
residual_risks: It is a model-specific two-witness result with changing bath, not a claim about timing at fixed generator, experimental observability, or all metrics.
